# Huawei VRP — GUI / CLI / SNMP Mapping

Per [gui-cli-snmp-unification.md](../../00-architecture/gui-cli-snmp-unification.md), every GUI action must be traceable to the literal CLI a human would type (echoed into the terminal) and/or a documented SNMP SET, never a hidden side-channel. VRP is an **immediate-apply** CLI (no candidate-config/commit step — see [overview.md](overview.md)), so "GUI as echoed in terminal" below is the literal command sequence, applied line-by-line as typed; **`save` is always a separate, explicit step** the GUI must trigger distinctly from the action itself.

| GUI Action | CLI as echoed in terminal | SNMP SET (MIB::object, OID) | Read-back / GUI sync source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enable port | `system-view`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1`<br>`undo shutdown` | `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus.<ifIndex> = up(1)` (`1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.7.<ifIndex>`) | `display interface brief` (admin/oper column) or `IF-MIB::ifOperStatus` GET for confirmed link state | SNMP SET path only if no live CLI session is open — CLI is the default per the unification doc. `ifIndex`→interface-name resolution via `ifName`/`ifDescr`, not cached across reboots. |
| Disable port | `system-view`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1`<br>`shutdown` | `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus.<ifIndex> = down(2)` | same as above | |
| Set interface description | `system-view`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1`<br>`description <text>` | `IF-MIB::ifAlias.<ifIndex> = "<text>"` (`1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18.<ifIndex>`) | `display interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1` or `ifAlias` GET | Confirm device-specific max length via that model's command reference before validating GUI input length client-side. |
| Set access VLAN (PVID) | `system-view`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1`<br>`port link-type access`<br>`port default vlan 10` | `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qPvid.<bridge-port>` — **confirmed SNMP-writable** (Phase 2 verification pass, 2026-07-16 — Huawei's own Q-BRIDGE-MIB reference states "only `dot1qPvid` can be modified" in that table; see [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md)). This is a genuine, working SNMP fallback for PVID/access-VLAN assignment specifically — **does not** extend to VLAN creation or trunk-allowed-list membership, both still unconfirmed. | `display vlan 10` or `display interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1` | Two-line CLI sequence — GUI must ensure `port link-type access` is issued (or already in effect) before `port default vlan`, and the session tracker must know the interface's current link-type context per the session-model doc. With the SNMP path now confirmed, SignalScope may use it as a fallback when no live CLI session is open, per the unification doc's standard rule — but only for this specific action among Huawei's VLAN-related actions. |
| Set trunk allowed VLANs | `system-view`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1`<br>`port link-type trunk`<br>`port trunk allow-pass vlan 10 to 20` | `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qVlanStaticEgressPorts`/`dot1qVlanStaticUntaggedPorts` bitmask SETs — **write support not independently confirmed**; treat as CLI-only until verified | `display vlan 10` (port membership) or `display interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1` | VLAN 1 is trunk-default-allowed on a fresh trunk port — GUI diffing logic should account for this default rather than reading its absence from an explicit `allow-pass` line as "VLAN 1 blocked." |
| Create VLAN | `system-view`<br>`vlan 10` (or `vlan batch 10 15 to 19` for several at once) | `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qVlanStaticRowStatus.<vlan-id> = createAndGo(4)` — **not independently confirmed for Huawei**; may require `HUAWEI-L2VLAN-MIB` instead | `display vlan` | `vlan batch` GUI-side maps to a single CLI line for multiple VLANs — if the GUI lets a user multi-select VLAN IDs to create at once, echo the single `vlan batch` line rather than one `vlan <n>` per ID, to keep the terminal a faithful record of what was actually sent. |
| Enable STP edge-port setting | `system-view`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1`<br>`stp edged-port enable` | No standard MIB object confirmed for this (BRIDGE-MIB's `dot1dStpPortTable` doesn't model edge-port/PortFast-equivalent state) — CLI-only action | `display stp interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1` | Requires global `stp enable` to be in effect first for the setting to have operational meaning, though the command itself can be entered regardless. |
| LACP / Eth-Trunk membership | `system-view`<br>`interface Eth-Trunk1`<br>`mode lacp-static`<br>`quit`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1`<br>`eth-trunk 1` | No standard SNMP write path confirmed (`IEEE8023-LAG-MIB` read-only support likely exists for state but not membership writes) — CLI-only action | `display eth-trunk 1` | Eth-Trunk must have no members when its mode is (re)set — GUI must sequence "remove existing members" before a mode change on an already-populated trunk, and reflect that constraint as a blocking validation rather than sending a command that will error. |
| Port security enable + max-MAC | `system-view`<br>`interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1`<br>`port-security enable`<br>`port-security max-mac-num 5` | No standard MIB write path confirmed — CLI-only action | `display port-security` | Mutually exclusive with `mac-limit maximum` on the same interface — GUI should surface this as a validation error rather than letting both be configured. |
| Save configuration | `save` (interactive Y/N [+ optional filename] prompt) | No SNMP equivalent confirmed (unlike Cisco's `CISCO-CONFIG-COPY-MIB` trigger-object pattern noted in `connectivity-methods.md`; Huawei's `HUAWEI-CONFIG-MAN-MIB` may offer one but its object-level detail wasn't confirmed in this research pass) | `display current-configuration` diffed against last-saved snapshot, or re-issuing `save` and observing the "already saved, nothing changed" vs. prompt behavior | This is the one action in this table that is **not** part of the immediate-apply config itself — it's the explicit persistence step. GUI's "Save" button must drive the CLI session through the interactive prompt (confirm Y, optionally supply filename), not just fire the bare command and assume success. |
| Configure SNMP community | `system-view`<br>`snmp-agent community read <name> mib-view <view-name>`<br>`snmp-agent community write <name> mib-view <view-name>` | N/A (this is SNMP-agent configuration itself, done via CLI/SSH — not something typically done via a self-referential SNMP SET) | `display snmp-agent community` | Always bind a `mib-view` explicitly rather than leaving it defaulted to `ViewDefault` if the intent is restricted access — see [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md) for the access-control model. |
| Configure SNMP trap target | `system-view`<br>`snmp-agent trap enable`<br>`snmp-agent target-host trap address udp-domain <ip> params securityname <string> v2c` | N/A | `display snmp-agent target-host` | `snmp-agent trap enable` is required globally (or per-feature) in addition to the target-host line, or no traps are actually sent — GUI must send/track both lines as a pair, not just the target-host line. |
| Configure `snmp-agent mib-view` access control | `system-view`<br>`snmp-agent mib-view included myview 1.3.6.1.2.1`<br>`snmp-agent mib-view excluded myview system.7` | N/A | `display snmp-agent mib-view <view-name>` | Distinctive VRP feature — see [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md#snmp-agent-mib-view--vrps-mib-access-control-model). GUI's SNMP-config screen for Huawei devices should expose view management as a first-class concept (not just community read/write toggles), since this is where write-SET failures for otherwise "write-permitted" communities/groups actually originate. |

## Rows marked "not independently confirmed"

**Update, Phase 2 verification pass (2026-07-16)**: `dot1qPvid` (access-VLAN/PVID assignment) is now confirmed writable — see that row above and [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md). This was the single highest-priority item in [`ROADMAP.md`](../../ROADMAP.md)'s verification backlog and is now resolved.

The remaining SNMP SET paths above (VLAN *creation*/trunk-allowed-list via `Q-BRIDGE-MIB` or `HUAWEI-L2VLAN-MIB`, STP edge-port, LACP membership, port-security, config-save trigger) are still unconfirmed as actually supported/writable on Huawei S-series devices — Huawei's MIB reference pages describe object *definitions* but no explicit "this object is writable via SNMP on S-series" statement was found for any of these in either the original or this follow-up research pass (several official Huawei doc pages are JS-rendered and not directly fetchable by automated tools, limiting this pass to search-engine-summary confirmation rather than a first-hand document read — see the confidence-tier note in [mib-reference.md](mib-reference.md)). Per [connectivity-methods.md](../../00-architecture/connectivity-methods.md)'s explicit warning, **treat all of these as CLI-only until verified against a live device or an authoritative Huawei write-support statement.**
